This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary angle degree right-triangle hypotenuse sine cosine tangent unit-circle quadrant atan2 angular-speed oscillation amplitude period >}}

## 4.1 Which way is the drone facing? Angles

- The **angle** of a direction is the turn from the +x axis, in
  **degrees** (°).
- 0° points right (+x), 90° up (+y), 180° left (−x), 270° down (−y).
- A positive angle turns **anticlockwise**; a negative angle turns
  clockwise. −45° is the same direction as 315°.
- A full turn is 360°. Two angles that differ by 360° give the same
  direction: 370° = 10°.
- Unity turns a 2D object anticlockwise for a positive angle too.

![Angles in game maths.](images/angle-dial.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
On a map, 0° is north and angles turn clockwise. In game maths, 0° is +x
and angles turn anticlockwise.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Draw five headings"}
On squared paper, draw the axes and arrows for 0°, 90°, 135°, 225° and −45°
(use the diagonals of the squares for 45°). Write the second name of each
angle, for example 270° = −90°.

::: {.check}
0° right, 90° up, 135° up-left, 225° down-left, −45° down-right (the last
three on the diagonals). Second names: 360°, −270°, −225°, −135°, 315°.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Headings"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="down (−y)|200°"}
A drone has the heading 90°. Which way does it fly?
:   up (+y)

    Why: 90° points along +y.

A drone has the heading 180°. Which way does it fly?
:   left (−x)

    Why: half a turn from +x: along −x.

Which angle is the same direction as −90°?
:   270°

    Why: −90° + 360° = 270°.

A turret faces 350° and turns 20° anticlockwise. Which angle does it face?
:   10°

    Why: 350° + 20° = 370°, and 370° − 360° = 10°.

On a map, east is 90°. Which angle is east in game maths?
:   0°

    Why: game maths starts at +x (east), so east is 0°.
:::
:::

## 4.2 How high is the ramp? Sine, cosine and tangent

- A **right triangle** has one angle of 90°.
- For the angle θ: the **hypotenuse** is the longest side, the
  **opposite** side is across from θ, the **adjacent** side is next to θ.
- sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse; cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse;
  tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
- So: opposite = hypotenuse × sin θ, adjacent = hypotenuse × cos θ.
- tan θ is the **slope**: how far up for 1 forward.

| θ | 0° | 30° | 45° | 60° | 90° |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sin θ | 0 | 0.5 | 0.71 | 0.87 | 1 |
| cos θ | 1 | 0.87 | 0.71 | 0.5 | 0 |
| tan θ | 0 | 0.58 | 1 | 1.73 | — |

- Ramp 10 m at 30°: height 10 × 0.5 = **5 m**, forward 10 × 0.87 =
  **8.7 m**.
- Hill 3 m up over 4 m forward (slope side 5 m): sin = 0.6, cos = 0.8,
  tan = 0.75.

![The ramp as a right triangle.](images/right-triangle.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Opposite and adjacent depend on the angle you look from.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The calculator of your phone"}
Open the calculator in scientific mode (DEG, not RAD). Compute sin 30°,
cos 30° and tan 45°, and compare with the table. Then compute the height of
a 10 m ramp at 20°: 10 × sin 20°.

::: {.check}
sin 30° = 0.5, cos 30° ≈ 0.87, tan 45° = 1. The ramp: about 10 × 0.34 =
3.4 m. If sin 30 gives −0.99, the calculator is in RAD mode.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The right triangle"}
Use the table above. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="opposite ÷ adjacent|20 m"}
sin θ is …
:   opposite ÷ hypotenuse

    Why: sine = opposite side ÷ hypotenuse.

A ramp is 10 m long and rises at 30°. How high is it?
:   5 m

    Why: height = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5.

A ramp is 10 m long and rises at 30°. How far forward does it reach?
:   8.7 m

    Why: forward = 10 × cos 30° = 10 × 0.87.

A hill rises 3 m over 4 m forward. What is tan θ, the slope?
:   0.75

    Why: tan = opposite ÷ adjacent = 3 ÷ 4.

Which side of a right triangle is the longest?
:   the hypotenuse

    Why: the hypotenuse is across from the 90° angle.
:::
:::

## 4.3 Every angle at once: the unit circle

- The **unit circle** has the radius 1 and the centre (0, 0).
- The point at the angle θ is **(cos θ, sin θ)**: cos is x, sin is y.
- 0°: (1, 0). 90°: (0, 1). 180°: (−1, 0). 270°: (0, −1).
- For larger angles, the same numbers come back with signs: 30° (0.87, 0.5),
  150° (−0.87, 0.5), 210° (−0.87, −0.5), 330° (0.87, −0.5).
- cos² θ + sin² θ = 1: (cos θ, sin θ) is always a **unit vector**.
- At 90° and 270°, cos θ = 0, so tan θ does not exist.

![The unit circle.](images/unit-circle.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The point is (cos θ, sin θ), not (sin θ, cos θ). At 90° it is (0, 1).
:::

{{< sim file="sims/unit-circle-lab.html" poster="sims/unit-circle-lab.png" title="Unit Circle Lab: cos, sin and tan for every angle" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Four points in Unit Circle Lab"}
In **Unit Circle Lab**, put the point at 30°, 150°, 210° and 330°. Write
cos θ and sin θ each time. What changes from row to row, and what stays the
same?

::: {.check}
30° (0.87, 0.5), 150° (−0.87, 0.5), 210° (−0.87, −0.5), 330° (0.87, −0.5):
the numbers stay; only the signs change.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · On the circle"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(1, 0)|(0.87, −0.5)"}
The point on the unit circle at 90°.
:   (0, 1)

    Why: (cos 90°, sin 90°) = (0, 1): straight up.

The point on the unit circle at 180°.
:   (−1, 0)

    Why: half a turn: straight left.

The point at 30° is (0.87, 0.5). The point at 150°?
:   (−0.87, 0.5)

    Why: the mirror across the y-axis: x changes sign.

At 210°, which signs do cos θ and sin θ have?
:   both negative

    Why: 210° is in quadrant III: left and down.

Why is (0.6, 0.8) on the unit circle?
:   0.36 + 0.64 = 1

    Why: 0.6² + 0.8² = 1: the point is 1 unit from the origin.
:::
:::

## 4.4 From an angle to a movement

- The direction at the angle θ is the unit vector **(cos θ, sin θ)**.
- Velocity = speed × direction (Lecture 2):
  **v = s (cos θ, sin θ) = (s cos θ, s sin θ)**.
- Drone at 30°, speed 10: 10 × (0.87, 0.5) = **(8.7, 5)**. After 2 s:
  (17.4, 10).
- Ball at 135°, speed 4: 4 × (−0.71, 0.71) ≈ **(−2.8, 2.8)**: left and up.
- Game code measures angles in **radians**, so it converts first:
  `Mathf.Sin(30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad)` gives 0.5.

![The drone flies at 30° with the speed 10.](images/angle-velocity.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not multiply the speed by the angle (10 × 30 = 300 is wrong). Multiply
the speed by cos θ and by sin θ.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Velocity from the unit circle"}
A boat sails at 60° with the speed 6. In **Unit Circle Lab**, read cos 60°
and sin 60°. Multiply both by 6. Check: is the length of your vector about
6?

::: {.check}
6 × (0.5, 0.87) ≈ (3, 5.2). Check: 3² + 5.2² ≈ 9 + 27 = 36 = 6².
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Velocity"}
Use the table of section 4.2. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(5, 8.7)|300"}
A drone flies at 30° with the speed 10. Its velocity?
:   (8.7, 5)

    Why: 10 × (0.87, 0.5) = (8.7, 5).

A drone flies at 45° with the speed 10. Its velocity?
:   (7.1, 7.1)

    Why: 10 × (0.71, 0.71) = (7.1, 7.1).

A drone flies at 90° with the speed 3. Its velocity?
:   (0, 3)

    Why: 3 × (0, 1) = (0, 3).

A boat sails at 60° with the speed 6. Its velocity?
:   about (3, 5.2)

    Why: 6 × (cos 60°, sin 60°) = 6 × (0.5, 0.87).

A ball moves at 135°. Which way does it go?
:   left and up

    Why: 135° is in quadrant II: x minus, y plus.
:::
:::

## 4.5 Which angle is the target at?

- A turret at (0, 0) must face a drone at d = (4, 4). Which angle?
- tan θ = d~y~ ÷ d~x~ = 1, so 45°. But (−4, −4) also gives 1: the
  division loses the signs.
- **atan2(y, x)** uses the signs of both parts. It gives the angle from
  −180° to 180°, right in every quadrant.
- (4, 4): 45°. (−4, 4): 135°. (−4, −4): −135°. (0, −3): −90°.

![Same slope, different angle.](images/atan2.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The order is (y, x). With (x, y), a drone at (4, 0) comes out at 90°
instead of 0°.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Angles on paper"}
On squared paper, mark a turret at (0, 0) and the targets (5, 0), (0, 4),
(−3, 3) and (−3, −3). Draw each vector d. Which quadrant is each target in,
and which angle does atan2 give? Use the axes and the 45° diagonals.

::: {.check}
(5, 0): 0°, on the x-axis. (0, 4): 90°, on the y-axis. (−3, 3): 135°,
quadrant II. (−3, −3): −135° (= 225°), quadrant III.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The angle to a target"}
The turret is at (0, 0). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="−45°|0°"}
A drone at (5, 5). Its angle?
:   45°

    Why: both parts equal and positive: the diagonal of quadrant I.

A drone at (−4, 4). Its angle?
:   135°

    Why: x minus, y plus: quadrant II, on the diagonal.

A drone at (−4, −4). Its angle?
:   −135°

    Why: both minus: quadrant III; atan2 gives −135° (= 225°).

A drone at (0, −3). Its angle?
:   −90°

    Why: straight down.

Why is tan alone not enough?
:   it loses the signs of x and y

    Why: (4, 4) and (−4, −4) give the same y ÷ x = 1.
:::
:::

## 4.6 Moving in a circle

- An orb circles a hero; a moon circles a planet.
- Position: **P(t) = C + r (cos θ, sin θ)**, with the centre C and the
  radius r.
- The angle grows at the **angular speed** ω: θ = ω × t.
- **Period**: one full turn takes T = 360° ÷ ω.
- C = (5, 5), r = 2, 90° per second: t = 0 (7, 5); 1 s (5, 7); 2 s (3, 5);
  3 s (5, 3); period 4 s.

![The orb circles C = (5, 5).](images/orbit.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Multiply (cos θ, sin θ) by the radius, then add the centre.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/wave-lab.html" poster="sims/wave-lab.png" title="Wave Lab: circle, bob and sweep" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · An orbit in Wave Lab"}
In **Wave Lab**, choose **Orbit**, the amplitude 2 (the radius) and the
period 4 s. Step to 0, 1, 2 and 3 s and write the positions. Then set the
period to 8 s: what is the angular speed?

::: {.check}
Wave Lab circles (0, 2): 0 s (2, 2); 1 s (0, 4); 2 s (−2, 2); 3 s (0, 0).
Period 8 s: 360° ÷ 8 = 45° per second.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Orbits"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(7, 5)|(5, 5)"}
C = (5, 5), r = 2, 90° per second. Where is the orb at 1 s?
:   (5, 7)

    Why: θ = 90°: (5, 5) + 2 × (0, 1).

The same orb at 2 s?
:   (3, 5)

    Why: θ = 180°: (5, 5) + 2 × (−1, 0).

An orb turns at 90° per second. Its period?
:   4 s

    Why: 360° ÷ 90° = 4 s.

A moon turns at 30° per second. Its period?
:   12 s

    Why: 360° ÷ 30° = 12 s.

Centre (0, 0), r = 4, angle 90°. The position?
:   (0, 4)

    Why: 4 × (cos 90°, sin 90°) = 4 × (0, 1).
:::
:::

## 4.7 Bobbing up and down: oscillating motion

- A coin bobs; a lift goes up and down. This is an **oscillation**: back
  and forth around a middle, again and again.
- **y(t) = c + A sin(360° × t ÷ T)**: middle c, **amplitude** A,
  **period** T.
- At a quarter of T: the top, c + A. At three quarters: the bottom,
  c − A. At 0, half and full T: the middle.
- A coin: middle 4, A = 1, T = 2 s: 0.5 s → **5** (top); 1.5 s → **3**
  (bottom).
- The same sine can make an **angle** swing: a searchlight sweeps with
  angle(t) = 45° × sin(360° × t ÷ 4), and the beam points along
  (cos angle, sin angle). At 1 s: 45°; at 3 s: −45°.

![A bobbing value: middle 2, amplitude 3, period 4 s.](images/sine-wave.png){width=90%}

![A searchlight sweeps from −45° to 45°.](images/searchlight.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The amplitude is half of the whole movement: with A = 3, a value moves
6 units from bottom to top.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The lift in Wave Lab"}
In **Wave Lab**, choose **Bob**, the amplitude 3 and the period 4 s. Step to
0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 s and write the heights. Then set the period to 8 s: when
is the lift at the top?

::: {.check}
Middle 2: 0 s 2; 1 s 5; 2 s 2; 3 s −1; 4 s 2. With the period 8 s, the top
comes at 2 s (a quarter of 8).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Bobbing"}
y = 2 + 3 sin(360° × t ÷ 4). Choose the right answer. You can use an answer
more than once.

::: {.match extra="3|8 s"}
The height at 1 s.
:   5

    Why: the angle is 90°: 2 + 3 × 1.

The height at 3 s.
:   −1

    Why: the angle is 270°: 2 + 3 × (−1).

The period.
:   4 s

    Why: T is the number under the division: 4 s.

How many units does the lift move from bottom to top?
:   6

    Why: from −1 to 5: twice the amplitude.

A searchlight: angle = 45° × sin(360° × t ÷ 4). The angle at 1 s?
:   45°

    Why: 45° × sin 90° = 45° × 1.

The same searchlight. How many degrees does the light cover in all?
:   90°

    Why: 45° to each side: from −45° to 45°.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Drone Drop {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Drone Drop** is a delivery game. The depot is at (0, 0). The drone flies at
the speed 10 for exactly 1 second, then drops the parcel. The player chooses
only the heading. Ana lives at (5, 8.7), Ben at (0, 10) and Cara at
(−7.1, 7.1). Each house is 10 units from the depot.

{{< sim file="sims/drone-drop.html" poster="sims/drone-drop.png" title="Drone Drop: choose the heading to each house" kind="game" height="780" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · Which heading?"}
Drone Drop: depot (0, 0), speed 10, 1 second. Ana (5, 8.7), Ben (0, 10),
Cara (−7.1, 7.1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="30°|180°"}
Which heading reaches Ana?
:   60°

    Why: (5, 8.7) = 10 × (0.5, 0.87) = 10 × (cos 60°, sin 60°).

Which heading reaches Ben?
:   90°

    Why: (0, 10) is straight up: 90°.

Which heading reaches Cara?
:   135°

    Why: (−7.1, 7.1) is up-left on the diagonal: 135°.

What is the velocity with the heading 60°?
:   (5, 8.7)

    Why: 10 × (cos 60°, sin 60°) = 10 × (0.5, 0.87).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 9 · New customers (harder)"}
Drone Drop: depot (0, 0), speed 10, 1 second. cos 30° = 0.87,
sin 30° = 0.5. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(5, −8.7)|(−5, −8.7)"}
The drone flies at 210°. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (−8.7, −5)

    Why: 10 × (−0.87, −0.5): quadrant III.

The drone flies at 330°. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (8.7, −5)

    Why: 10 × (0.87, −0.5): quadrant IV.

A customer lives at (0, −10). Which heading?
:   270°

    Why: straight down is 270°.

The drone flies at 90° for only 0.5 seconds. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (0, 5)

    Why: half of (0, 10) per second: (0, 5).

In Unity, which line makes the heading 30° ready for `Mathf.Cos`?
:   30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad

    Why: Unity's Mathf.Cos takes radians.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Angles start at +x and grow anticlockwise; 360° is a full turn.
- In a right triangle: sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.
- The point at θ on the unit circle is (cos θ, sin θ). Velocity = speed × (cos θ, sin θ).
- atan2(y, x) gives the angle of a vector in every quadrant.
- A circle: P = C + r (cos ωt, sin ωt). A bob: y = c + A sin(360° × t ÷ T).
